semantic_findings: The entry is a borrowed global-slot reader: one 32-bit load, one return, no validation and no reference counting. It is a getter, not a service locator with behaviour.

0x0167eb08 is word 18 (table offset 0x48) of a CONTIGUOUS 43-word singleton slot table at 0x0167eac0 spanning 0x0167eac0..0x0167eb68 (168 bytes), with no gap and no duplicate; the 43 accessors of the block map onto the 43 slots bijectively.

The slot has exactly one direct reader (this load) and zero direct writers in the whole image, confirmed both by the committed datarefs export and by an independent whole-file byte scan. Absence of a direct writer is not an immutability claim.

The whole slot block lies in .data's loader-zeroed tail (section offsets 0x572ac0..0x572b68, all past SizeOfRawData 0xc4c00), so no image initializer exists for any of the 43 words and the zero returned by an unpublished slot is the loader's, not a special case.
The returned word is consumed as a POINTER, not compared as a scalar: one caller moves it straight into ECX as a receiver (0x00bf6f72) and one pushes it straight as a stack argument (0x00b5feeb).

The class of the object is UNKNOWN. The SDK import names 0x0167eb0c (cStarManager::Get at 0x00b3d3a0) and 0x0167eb60 (cGameNounManager::Get at 0x00b3d400) in the same table and leaves 0x0167eb08, 0x0167eb00 and 0x0167eb04 unnamed; adjacency in the table is not identity, and this is an UNNAMED accessor.

The ABI record abstains from naming a convention and reports cdecl, stdcall, thiscall and fastcall as byte-identical, which is correct for a zero-parameter entry; this package models it as a plain zero-parameter entry and picks none.
summary: FUN_00b3d390 is a complete six-byte borrowed global-slot reader: MOV EAX,dword ptr ds:[0x0167eb08]; RET. No branch, call, flag test, store or validation, zero parameters, no receiver, zero callee cleanup. Staged as simulator_slot_getter_00b3d390 with a 10-group model test, green under g++ and clang++ -m32 -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror, and refuted by all seven external perturbations of the body. The slot is word 18 (table offset 0x48) of a contiguous 43-word singleton table at 0x0167eac0 whose 43 accessors map onto it bijectively, it lies in .data's loader-zeroed tail, and it has exactly one direct reader (this load) with zero direct writers in the pinned image. The returned word is demonstrably an object pointer (one caller moves it into ECX as a receiver, one pushes it as an argument) but NO field offset and NO class are claimed, because no sampled caller reaches an offset - weaker pointee evidence than sibling 0x00b3d380, and deliberately not strengthened by invention.

unresolved_questions: What class does the word at 0x0167eb08 point to? The SDK import leaves this slot, and 0x0167eb00 and 0x0167eb04, unnamed, and no committed research note names it. This is the single biggest gap and the reason the pointee type is opaque with no modelled extent.

Is 0x0167eb08 related to the SDK-named neighbours 0x0167eb0c (cStarManager::Get) and 0x0167eb60 (cGameNounManager::Get), and to the alternate slots 0x0167eae0 and 0x0167eae4 Phase 0 already closed? Adjacency in one table is not evidence of aliasing, and nothing here claims or denies it. The root closure's open alternate-vs-canonical question does not currently list this slot.
Who publishes 0x0167eb08, when, and how is it torn down and reset? There is no direct writer anywhere in the image and the slot is loader-zeroed, so publication is necessarily indirect or bulk.

Is the returned pointer ever null at a real callsite, and what do callers do then? None of the sampled sites null-tests the result, so no null contract is claimed in either direction - only that a stored zero is returned as a stored zero, which is what the body does.
Does the returned pointer need an AddRef, and if so by whom? The body has no room for a reference call and no writer is known, so ownership is undetermined.

Of the 63 distinct callers, only 0x00b5fde0 and 0x00bdc1a0's neighbourhoods were read by disassembly; the remaining 61 were counted from the edge sidecar and not classified by hand, because fan-in is not semantic evidence.

Promotion is blocked by a validator limitation rather than a package defect (FIELDS/OFFSETS cannot score a global-slot load). An integrator must either promote by review or add a global-slot arm to that check; tools/** was not modified.
